title: A deposit above the total leaves the exact customer credit
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user. That role holds every permission, including Part sales -> Create & Edit and Invoicing & payments -> Create & Edit. Numeric-accuracy case.
  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: top menu Customers -> New Customer, enter a Name (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair") and click Save.
  3. A part sale whose deposit exceeds its total. Seed: top menu Parts -> Part Sales -> New Part Sale (pick the customer, Save); in the Add Part dialog enter Description "Water Pump", Quantity 1, Vendor = a test vendor, Sell Price $517.55 -> Save & Close (with GST 5% the total is $543.43); Finance tab -> Add Deposit -> Deposit Amount $600.00, Payment Method "Cash" -> Record Deposit. Click Authorize, Order and Receive the part (in the Receive parts dialog type a part number and Cost, then Receive Parts). Compute 600.00 - 543.43 by hand.
custom_steps:
1. With the $600.00 deposit on the $543.43 sale (or after returning a core drops the total below the deposit), on the Finance tab click Create Invoice.
  2. Read the invoice state, its balance, and the customer credit produced; compare the surplus to your hand calculation.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The invoice is settled to zero and marked Paid (not Partially Paid), and the surplus becomes a customer credit of $56.57 (600.00 - 543.43).
  • The same holds when returning a core reduces the total below a deposit already taken: the surplus (deposit minus the new lower total) becomes a customer credit; no money is lost and nothing is refused.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667; story SV-10269; Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 8; design boards Document_*/Tax_* (exact figures shown on the canvas); read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-E1: “the invoice is settled to zero, it is marked Paid rather than Partially Paid, and the surplus becomes a customer credit”
  • S1-E3: “If a deposit has already been taken and returning a core drops the sale total below the deposit, the surplus becomes a customer credit when the sale is invoiced. No money is lost and nothing is refused”

Last checked against build v26.40.7-7ffda69 on 10/5/2026.
